name: Victoria Park
summary: A large park in Tower Hamlets, landscaped in 1842, with two lakes and a boating pond. Time Out says summer festivals such as Field Day and All Points East often take it over.

music.notes: Large summer festivals, with Time Out naming Field Day and All Points East, and an annual programme called In the Neighbourhood that includes live music, sport and family theatre.

crowd: Time Out says it attracts East Londoners in large numbers whatever the weather.

accessibility.notes: Both community buildings in the park have step-free access, and a Changing Places toilet has been installed. Blue Badge drivers are encouraged to use the disabled bays in the two main car parks.

evidence.quote: Stretched over a huge 86.18 hectares, this swath of the outdoors is nestled entirely in Tower Hamlets
originally landscaped by the famous architect Sir James Pennethorne in 1842
Victoria Park boasts two expansive lakes (one with a Chinese pagoda island), a boating pond and lots of wonderful activities for youngsters.
In the summer it’s often taken over by festivals like Field Day and All Points East.
Known as the ‘People’s Park’, Victoria Park is one of London’s favourite open spaces.
attracts East London dwellers in their masses, rain or shine
IN THE NEIGHBOURHOOD makes its annual return to Victoria Park
From Live Music, to Sport & Fitness Sessions, Family Theatre Shows
All Victoria Park's public toilets have an accessible cubicle and both our cafés are accessible for wheelchair users.
Both our community buildings offer step-free access.
We have installed a new changing places toilet facility at Victoria Park.
we strongly encourage Blue Badge drivers to make use of the designated disabled parking bays located in our two main car parks.
Victoria Park opens at 7am and closes at dusk, 365 days a year.
